findings.title: RSA token-signing private key committed to the repository and used as the live signing credential
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: The committed full RSA private JWK is loaded unconditionally via AddDeveloperSigningCredential while key management is disabled. The diff deletes tempkey.jwk, drops its Content Include from Identity.API.csproj, gitignores the name, and replaces the loader with a development-only in-memory credential (persistKey:false) plus a non-development AddSigningCredential(LoadPkcs12FromFile(...)) path that fails closed when config is missing.
findings.variants_checked: Only one signing-credential call site and only one .jwk file in the tree; AppHost passes no signing material; ServiceDefaults validation needed no change for this root cause.
findings.bypass_considered: A Development deployment now gets a fresh unknown in-memory key, so the old committed kid no longer validates; non-Development without configured certificate throws at startup. Residual: rotate and purge the key from history and published artifacts.
findings.test_note: Added IdentityApiDoesNotContainASigningKeyFile asserting no *.jwk under src/Identity.API.
findings.review_reason: Deletes the committed key and its build-output copy and replaces the unconditional developer credential with dev-only ephemeral material plus a fail-closed production certificate path; no checks removed. Remaining work is operational key rotation/history purge, plus a BOM and a brittle CallerFilePath-based test.

findings.title: JWT bearer disables audience validation, so any token from the IdP is accepted by every API
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Michael Stonis (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: AddDefaultAuthentication sets the per-service Audience then disables ValidateAudience, so tokens minted for another API or client ID tokens are accepted. The diff flips ValidateAudience to true, making the already-configured audience authoritative.
findings.variants_checked: Audience values in Basket/Ordering/Webhooks appsettings match the IdP API resources; WebApp requests both orders and basket, so its token still works; no service forwards a token across APIs.
findings.bypass_considered: ID tokens (aud = client id) and tokens for a different API are now rejected; a missing audience fails closed because ValidateAudience defaults to requiring one.
findings.review_reason: One-line flip re-enables audience validation using the value already read from required config, matching the IdP's disjoint API resources. No in-repo flow needs a cross-audience token; remaining https-metadata and fail-open issues are separate findings.

findings.title: Received-webhook token column is rendered to unauthenticated visitors
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Steve Sanderson (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: ReceivedMessages renders hook.Token and Home.razor:22 invokes it outside the AuthorizeView on the anonymous / route. The diff wraps the component body in AuthorizeView/NotAuthorized and applies the same gate to the AddWebhook form that pre-fills the same secret.
findings.variants_checked: ReceivedMessages fixed; RegisteredHooks already behind AuthorizeView; AddWebhook same-secret exposure gated; endpoints do not render the token.
findings.bypass_considered: A page-level [Authorize] would be inert because Routes.razor uses RouteView with no fallback policy, so the guard is an explicit AuthorizeView inside the component.
findings.test_note: Added ReceivedMessagesDoesNotRenderTokensToAnonymousVisitors using HtmlRenderer with an anonymous principal.
findings.review_reason: Wrapping the grid restores the same AuthorizeView boundary the sibling component already has, closing the token render for anonymous circuits. The AddWebhook hunk is off the call path but fixes the same secret exposure at an ungated page, so the patch is complete rather than narrowly scoped.

findings.title: GET /api/orders/{orderId} returns any order without an ownership check
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Srushti (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: The query filters only on order id and returns the full shipping address and items. The diff adds userId to GetOrderAsync and filters on Buyer.IdentityGuid, threading the authenticated identity from the endpoint; foreign ids collapse to the existing NotFound path.
findings.variants_checked: GetOrderAsync fixed; GetOrdersFromUserAsync already scoped; GetCardTypes has no owner; cancel/ship are separate findings.
findings.bypass_considered: A null or empty sub matches no buyer and returns 404; Buyer is a mapped navigation so the predicate is evaluated in SQL, and the endpoint group is already authenticated.
findings.test_note: Added Get_order_passes_authenticated_user_to_query and updated the two mock signatures.
findings.review_reason: Adds the ownership predicate at the data-access layer, mirroring the already-correct list query, so a foreign id is indistinguishable from a missing one. No parsing or validation weakened; residual gaps are a missing explicit null-identity guard and no foreign-id integration test.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can cancel any other user's order
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Rob Conery (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Cancel loads the order by the body-supplied number and cancels it without comparing the caller's sub. The diff adds an ownership gate in CancelOrderAsync using IIdentityService and a new OrderBelongsToUserAsync predicate on Buyer.IdentityGuid, returning a uniform 404 before the command is dispatched. The shared handler is deliberately untouched because the payment-failure broker path also cancels orders with no user context.
findings.variants_checked: Cancel fixed; GetOrderAsync and ShipOrderAsync are separate findings; the broker-driven cancel path stays functional; the new predicate mirrors GetOrdersFromUserAsync.
findings.bypass_considered: Spoofing buyer fields is impossible because the command carries only OrderNumber and identity comes from the sub claim; replaying an x-requestid does not re-dispatch.
findings.test_note: Added Cancel_order_owned_by_another_user_returns_not_found and updated the functional expectation from 500 to 404.
findings.review_reason: The guard runs before command construction and authorizes on the server-derived sub via a predicate that reuses the same Buyer.IdentityGuid join as the list query. Leaving the shared handler untouched is correct because the broker path cancels without a user. Only nits are a ProblemHttpResult instead of a typed NotFound and no log on the denied branch.

findings.title: CreateOrder trusts body-supplied UserId instead of the JWT sub claim
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Rob Conery (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: CreateOrder builds the command from body-supplied UserId/UserName while IIdentityService is unused, and the value drives the buyer identity and basket-clearing event. The diff derives userId/userName from the authenticated principal, rejects a missing subject, and removes UserId/UserName/Buyer from CreateOrderRequest; the handler prefers the principal.
findings.variants_checked: Create endpoint fixed; draft endpoint never writes identity; basket and webhooks already use the sub claim.
findings.bypass_considered: Sending victim userId/userName/buyer fields is ignored because the properties no longer exist on the server DTO and the command is built from claims; a token without sub is rejected 400. Residual in-process callers with no HttpContext fall back to the command value.
findings.test_note: Added Create_order_uses_authenticated_user_identity and updated the functional constructor.
findings.review_reason: Removes the spoofable body fields and sources identity from the validated sub claim, with a fail-closed guard. The handler hunk is redundant and its fallback fails open, but it is on the same path and unreachable from the API once the endpoint guard is in place.

findings.title: Order item prices and quantities are accepted from the client request, allowing arbitrary order totals
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Client unit prices flow straight into the persisted order and total. The diff adds ICatalogPriceService/CatalogPriceService to fetch authoritative prices, has CreateOrderCommandHandler resolve them before clearing the basket, fail closed on unknown products or invalid units, and persist catalog prices instead of item.UnitPrice; AppHost adds a catalog reference.
findings.variants_checked: Create and draft paths checked; the draft path remains a preview; cancel/ship carry no prices; the handler is the persistence choke point.
findings.bypass_considered: Duplicate ids collapse to one catalog price per product and unknown products are rejected before any order row or basket-clearing event is written. Residual: Units is still client-chosen but can only raise the total, and stock validation bounds it.
findings.test_note: Added Handle_prices_order_items_from_the_catalog (0.01 client price vs 99.95 catalog) and a stub price service for the functional fixture.
findings.review_reason: The handler substitutes the catalog price at the AddOrderItem call and rejects unknown or invalid items before basket clearing, so the client value no longer reaches the order total. Catalog lookups use integer ids and fail closed on partial or error responses; only nits are an HTTP call inside the DB transaction and a dead null-coalescing guard.

findings.title: Persistent blind SSRF: stored DestUrl is POSTed without re-validation and redirects are followed
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Stored DestUrl is POSTed with no delivery-time validation while the default client follows redirects. The diff adds a shared validator, validates before dispatch, registers a named client with AllowAutoRedirect=false, UseProxy=false and a ConnectCallback that re-resolves and only connects to public addresses, and applies the same client to the grant tester.
findings.variants_checked: Sender and grant tester both use the safe client; other clients use fixed internal base addresses.
findings.bypass_considered: Redirect and proxy pivots are closed; DNS rebinding is closed because ConnectCallback connects to the specific validated IP. Residual: a public IP that the platform NATs inward, or IPv4-translated IPv6 forms not matched by the ::/96 test.
findings.test_note: Added WebhookSenderSsrfTests asserting a stored metadata DestUrl never reaches the handler.
findings.review_reason: Validation runs before dispatch and ConnectCallback re-resolves and pins the public address at connect time, closing the rebind/redirect/proxy bypasses. No validation is weakened; the grant-tester hunk is the same SSRF class on the same subscription flow and reuses the safe client.

findings.title: Logout failure leaves access/refresh tokens in SecureStorage; post-logout redirect is unregistered
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Michael Stonis (4 of 4 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: SignOutAsync returns on LogoutAsync error before the only token wipe, the post-logout URI mismatches the registered value, and the caller ignores the result. The diff clears the token in a finally block, converts provider errors into a false result, appends /Account/Redirecting to the post-logout URI, and surfaces a failure alert.
findings.variants_checked: Sign-in, refresh, mock service and the profile caller checked; the browser callback activity has no path restriction so the extra path is still delivered.
findings.bypass_considered: All provider outcomes (error, cancel, missing endpoint, exception) now reach the finally and clear the token. Residual: if the keystore write itself throws, the token remains; a dedicated remove path with retry is a follow-up.
findings.test_note: Added SignOutClearsStoredTokenWhenProviderLogoutFailsTest using MockSettingsService and a failing override.
findings.review_reason: Clearing the stored token in finally eliminates the masked failure where an errored LogoutAsync returned early, and the redirect hunk matches the server registration. The caller now surfaces the failure; only noise is the broad catch and the test seam.

findings.title: Full raw integration-event bodies (buyer name, identity GUID) are written to span tags and logs
findings.owner_hint: top committer: iem365-michael (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Line 161 tags every consumed body and line 172 logs it on failure; events carry BuyerName and BuyerIdentityGuid. The diff replaces the body tag with the byte size, removes the body from the warning log, and stops embedding it in the fake-exception message, while leaving decode and dispatch unchanged.
findings.variants_checked: ProcessEvent already logs only the event name; DeserializeMessage does not log; the remaining body sinks were the tag, the exception text and the warning.
findings.bypass_considered: Exception text still flows into span exception tags, but the self-generated exception no longer contains the body; a JsonException leaks position, not content.
findings.test_note: No suitable test project exists for EventBusRabbitMQ; suggested a broker-free unit test asserting no message tag and size metadata.
findings.review_reason: All three body sinks in OnMessageReceived are replaced with non-identifying metadata while decode, dispatch, and the fake-exception trigger are unchanged. No new input surface and no validation weakened.

findings.title: Expected webhook token is logged in cleartext on every unauthenticated request
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Steve Sanderson (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: The Information-level log writes both the caller token and the configured expected secret before the check, on every anonymous request. The diff removes both secret arguments and logs only whether validation is enabled, leaving the comparison untouched.
findings.variants_checked: No other copy of the leaking message exists; other webhook log sites carry no secret.
findings.bypass_considered: Deleting the arguments means the values never enter ILogger state, so no provider or exporter can recover them. The separate grant-tester log leak is its own finding.
findings.test_note: Added WebhookEndpointDoesNotLogTokenValues with a capturing logger provider asserting neither secret appears.
findings.review_reason: The production hunk removes both the caller and configured token from the Information log while leaving validation intact, eliminating the sink rather than masking it. The added test uses the file's existing TestServer pattern and asserts neither secret is captured.

findings.title: GET /Account/Logout signs the user out without a prompt, enabling logout CSRF
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: ShowLogoutPrompt=false makes the anonymous GET handler call the POST logout action in-process, bypassing antiforgery. The diff restores the prompt default and only auto-signs-out when the user is authenticated, a logoutId was supplied, and the prompt was suppressed.
findings.variants_checked: Other GET handlers are read-only or begin external auth; all state-changing POSTs keep antiforgery.
findings.bypass_considered: A bare cross-site GET now renders the prompt and the follow-up POST needs an antiforgery token. Residual: a valid RP-initiated logoutId with ShowSignoutPrompt=false still auto-signs-out by design.
findings.test_note: Added LogoutPromptStaysEnabled asserting the restored default.
findings.review_reason: Restoring the prompt default fixes the root cause that made the GET handler sign out unconditionally; the added guard only strengthens the condition. The logoutId check is effectively dead given the prompt-suppression path already requires a context, and the test only asserts the static default.

findings.title: Catalog write endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE) are completely unauthenticated and reachable through the external mobile BFF
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Mike Kistler (3 of 3 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Root cause is Catalog.API never calling AddDefaultAuthentication (Program.cs) and mapping the four write endpoints without RequireAuthorization (CatalogApi.cs:100,105,110,114); the BFF merely exposes it. The diff registers AddDefaultAuthentication, adds the required Identity:Audience plus Identity__Url from AppHost, attaches RequireAuthorization to exactly the PUT/POST/DELETE endpoints, and relaxes two OpenAPI GetRequiredSection("Scopes") calls so the service can boot without a per-API Scopes map. Reads stay anonymous.
findings.variants_checked: All four catalog write mappings fixed; Ordering/Webhooks groups already gated; Basket gRPC out of this surface; BFF route left as a forwarder because the resource now returns 401.
findings.bypass_considered: Anonymous PUT/POST/DELETE via the BFF now hits authorization middleware before model binding and returns 401; only a valid low-privilege JWT remains (audience validation is a separate finding).
findings.test_note: Added CatalogWriteEndpointsRejectAnonymousRequests (expects 401) plus a test-only AutoAuthorizeMiddleware so existing happy-path write tests still authenticate.
findings.review_reason: Core fix is correct and well-scoped, but both ServiceDefaults hunks are off the call path and delete a fail-fast config check for all services; adding a Scopes section to Catalog appsettings would keep the guard. The test shim also authenticates by default, so the new test only checks endpoint metadata.

findings.title: Any authenticated customer can ship any order
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Rob Conery (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Ship is gated only by bare authentication and the handler ships whichever order number the body supplies, despite being documented as an administrator action. The diff registers an AdminOnly policy requiring the admin role and adds RequireAuthorization("AdminOnly") to the ship endpoint.
findings.variants_checked: Ship fixed; cancel and by-id read have different root causes left to their own fixes; no other admin-only operation exists in the group; Webhooks handlers filter by caller id.
findings.bypass_considered: Authorization evaluates validated JWT claims before model binding, so body order numbers cannot influence it; a forged role claim is blocked by issuer/signature validation.
findings.test_note: Added ShipOrderRequiresAdminRole (403 for customer) and extended the test middleware with a role claim defaulting to admin.
findings.review_reason: Right layer, but nothing issues the admin role: ProfileService emits no role claim and UsersSeed assigns no roles, so RequireRole("admin") would 403 every caller and permanently disable shipping. The test only passes because AutoAuthorizeMiddleware defaults every request to admin.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /add-webhook page renders the configured webhook validation token into the HTML
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Steve Sanderson (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: OnInitialized copies WebhookClientOptions.Token into a field bound to an input, so it is emitted during prerender to anonymous visitors. The diff removes that assignment and resolves the token server-side inside RegisterAsync, keeping it out of component state and the DOM.
findings.variants_checked: AddWebhook fixed; RegisteredHooks and ReceivedMessages are separate render sites; endpoints use the token server-side only.
findings.bypass_considered: Even if the page were reachable, the configured token is no longer held in a bound field or rendered, so the HTML cannot disclose it.
findings.test_note: No test added: no WebhookClient test project exists and the change is a one-field removal.
findings.review_reason: The token-removal hunks are correct root-cause fixes, but the patch also adds [Authorize], an unrelated policy change that is inert anyway because Routes.razor uses RouteView instead of AuthorizeRouteView. Drop that hunk or ship it with the router change.

findings.title: Webhook signing token written to logs in cleartext at Information level
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Both Information-level messages log the caller and expected webhook tokens verbatim. The diff replaces the token values with booleans for supplied/received/matched.
findings.variants_checked: WebhooksSender logs only destination and type; API handlers do not log the token; validation messages carry no values.
findings.bypass_considered: The receiver's own proxy or non-default header-recording instrumentation can still log the X-eshop-whtoken header; that is receiver-side and outside this file.
findings.test_note: No test added: no unit-test project exists for Webhooks.API and the service is internal; the functional fixture replaces the real tester.
findings.review_reason: Hunk 1 fixes the leak, but hunk 2 still logs {TokenReceived}, which is the receiver's echo of the same shared secret, so the credential remains in logs on the success path and user-controlled header content still reaches the logger. Log only the TokenMatched boolean and fix the IsNullOrEmpty/IsNullOrWhiteSpace mismatch.

findings.title: All confidential OIDC clients share the literal client secret "secret", including the public MAUI client
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Michael Stonis (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: All three clients register the same literal secret and the MAUI binary ships it, with webapp also disabling PKCE. The diff loads per-client secrets from ClientSecrets:{clientId} with fail-closed lookup, makes MAUI a public client (no secret, PKCE retained), enables PKCE for webapp, and reads the relying-party secrets from configuration.
findings.variants_checked: Server and both relying parties plus the MAUI default changed; swagger clients are intentionally public; no other committed client-secret literals found.
findings.bypass_considered: MAUI remains a public client whose client_id and custom scheme are known; PKCE stops code interception but not a malicious app starting its own flow. Distinct secrets rely on operational config.
findings.test_note: Added ConfidentialClientsUseConfiguredSecretsAndPkce and extended the existing config dictionary.
findings.review_reason: Secret removal is root-cause, but the patch adds required ClientSecrets/ClientSecret keys without supplying them in appsettings or AppHost, so Identity.API and both relying parties throw at startup; the unit fixture hides it with dummy values. It also mixes in webapp PKCE changes that belong to a separate finding.

findings.title: Authenticated user can force server-side requests to arbitrary hosts
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: The grant tester fetches a caller-supplied URL after only a format check and a same-origin comparison of two attacker URLs. The diff adds a WebhookUrlValidator policy (http/https only, no userinfo, block loopback/private/link-local/metadata/numeric hosts/single-label names), applies it at validation and at both egress points, and disables auto-redirects on a named client.
findings.variants_checked: Grant tester, sender, and request validation all use the validator; other outbound clients use fixed base addresses.
findings.bypass_considered: Validation is pre-DNS, so a dotted attacker hostname resolving to an internal address still reaches the sink; closing that needs resolve-time pinning. Redirect pivots are blocked.
findings.test_note: Added WebhookUrlValidatorTests with public and internal URL cases.
findings.review_reason: The allowlist and redirect suppression are the right layer, but IsAllowed accepts any dotted hostname without resolving it, so a name pointing at 169.254.169.254 still reaches SendAsync; IsPublicAddress only applies to literals. Move validation to resolution/connect time with a pinned ConnectCallback, and keep the sibling sender hunks separate.

findings.title: Full PAN and CVV are written to logs on order creation
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Rob Conery (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
findings.rationale: Line 134 logs the raw CreateOrderRequest record, whose synthesized ToString prints PAN and CVV before masking. The diff logs only UserId and adds ToString overrides that mask the PAN and CVV on CreateOrderRequest and CreateOrderCommand.
findings.variants_checked: The warning sink and command log sites checked; other order commands carry no card data; MediatR behaviors log the command object.
findings.bypass_considered: Serilog-style object destructuring ignores ToString and would still print CardSecurityNumber; there is no such sink in the repo today, so the masking is defense-in-depth rather than a complete guarantee.
findings.test_note: Added Create_order_does_not_log_pan_or_cvv capturing logger arguments and asserting PAN/CVV are absent.
findings.review_reason: The line-134 change is the correct root-cause fix, but the patch also modifies the unrelated CreateOrderCommand class and relies on ToString masking, which serializer sinks bypass; the CVV still enters the command unmasked and is logged via {@Command}. The test asserts ToString rather than the rendered template.
